items.prompt: A mobile game shows a live global top-100 and each player's own rank; 50 000 score updates per second come from 20 million players.
items.why: A ranking updated in real time and read by rank → a sorted set (ZINCRBY, ZREVRANGE, ZREVRANK), each O(log n) in memory. A SQL ORDER BY over 20M rows per read won't keep up.

items.prompt: Product pages are read 100× more than they change, and the catalogue database's p99 of 40 ms must drop under 10 ms; what's the first idea to name?
items.why: The question is the pattern: a read-heavy workload tolerating some staleness → a cache in front of the database. Redis may be where it lives, but lead with cache-aside, TTL and invalidation.

items.prompt: A chat backend needs to know which of 200 gateway servers each connected device is attached to; a device that stops sending heartbeats should drop out within a minute.
items.why: Small, hot, shared state that must vanish on its own → a key per device with a 60 s TTL refreshed by heartbeats. etcd is built for small, strongly consistent config, not millions of keys updated every few seconds.

items.prompt: Store 30 TB of user orders that are the source of truth, queried by user_id with single-digit-ms latency, and that must survive the loss of a data centre.
items.why: Too big for RAM and must be durable → a disk-backed, replicated key-value store. Redis' async replication and memory limit make it the wrong home for the only copy.

items.prompt: An API must cap each API key at 1 000 requests per minute across 40 stateless gateway instances, checked on every request in about a millisecond.
items.why: A shared counter per key and window, updated on every request and expiring by itself → INCR + EXPIRE (or a Lua token bucket) in Redis. A SQL row per client can't take hundreds of thousands of increments per second.

items.prompt: Order events must be kept for 7 days so that the billing and analytics services can each read them at their own pace and replay after a bug.
items.why: Durable, replayable history read by independent consumer groups → a log. Redis pub/sub drops messages for subscribers that aren't connected right now.

items.prompt: A ride app receives every driver's GPS position every 4 seconds and must answer 'drivers within 2 km of this rider' in a few ms.
items.why: A tiny, constantly overwritten working set queried by radius → GEOADD / GEOSEARCH in memory. Re-indexing a search engine or a table 250 000 times a second is the expensive way to do it.

items.prompt: Two services must update an account balance and write a ledger entry together, with constraints, and ad-hoc reporting queries later.
items.why: Multi-row transactions, constraints and ad-hoc queries over durable data → a relational database. Redis has no joins or secondary indexes and can lose the last second of writes.
